06-2.solution: The mirror swaps the 3 and the 9, so the hour hand appears at 9 and the minute hand stays at 12: \(9:00\).

06-3.solution: For a 12-hour clock, mirror time \(= 11:60 - \) the time shown: \(11:60 - 4:20 = 7:40\).

06-4.solution: For a 12-hour clock, mirror time \(= 11:60 - \) the time shown: \(11:60 - 7:25 = 4:35\).

06-5.solution: For a 12-hour clock, mirror time \(= 11:60 - \) the time shown: \(11:60 - 2:15 = 9:45\).

06-6.solution: For a 12-hour clock, mirror time \(= 11:60 - \) the time shown: \(11:60 - 8:30 = 3:30\).

06-7.solution: The actual time is found the same way as the image: \(11:60 - 1:30 = 10:30\).

06-8.solution: The actual time is found the same way as the image: \(11:60 - 10:20 = 1:40\).

06-9.solution: The actual time is found the same way as the image: \(11:60 - 7:20 = 4:40\).

06-10.solution: The actual time is found the same way as the image: \(11:60 - 1:15 = 10:45\).

06-11.solution: The actual time is found the same way as the image: \(11:60 - 10:15 = 1:45\).

06-13.solution: For a 12-hour clock, mirror time \(= 11:60 - \) the time shown: \(11:60 - 9:10 = 2:50\).

06-14.solution: The actual time is found the same way as the image: \(11:60 - 3:40 = 8:20\).

06-16.solution: Two and a quarter hours ago the actual time was \(11:60 - 1:30 = 10:30\). Now it is \(10:30 + 2:15 = 12:45\).

06-17.solution: The mirror image of a time between 4 and 5 is \(11:60 - 4{:}m = 7{:}(60 - m)\), a time between 7 and 8. So the image is never between 4 and 5.

06-21.solution: The mirror image of \(x:y\) on a 12-hour clock is \(11:60 - x:y\): subtract \(x:y\) from \(11:60\).

06-22.solution: The mirror reflects the dial across the 12-6 line, so a time \(t\) minutes before 12:00 appears as one \(t\) minutes after 12:00. The real time is \(t\) minutes after \(12:00\).
